terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the tests here and read what they say.

tasks.title: Test a count that comes later
tasks.description:
`countOf(item)` reads `shed.json` and answers later with the number of that item in the shed. In the `count` block, test that it gives the right number for an item the shed has some of.

Check runs your tests on the working code and on versions that give the count as text, or answer 0 for everything. A test in this block must pass on the first and fail on the others.
nextSteps: Pick an item in `shed.json` that the shed has some of, and note its count.
Wait for `countOf` with `await` and compare the answer with your count.
hints: If Received says `Promise {}`, the test compared the promise, not the number it brings later.
A test can only use `await` when its own function is `async`. The lesson shows where both words go.
Write `expect(await countOf('leeks')).toBe(14)` inside a test whose function starts with `async () =>`.

tasks.title: Test the yes and the no from canPack
tasks.description:
`canPack(items, boxes)` answers later with `true` when the shed has at least `boxes` of every item on the list, and `false` when any of them runs short. In the `enough` block, test one list it can pack and one it cannot, where the item that runs short is not the first on the list.

Check runs your tests on the working code and on versions that say no to everything, or only look at the first item. A test in this block must pass on the first and fail on the others.
nextSteps: Pick a list and a number of boxes that every item has enough for.
Pick a list where a later item runs short, and expect a no.
Check each answer with `resolves`, and run the tests.
hints: A test with only a yes, or with the short item first, passes even when `canPack` skips the rest of the list.
`resolves` goes between `expect(...)` and the matcher, and the whole line needs `await` in front of it.
Write `await expect(canPack(['potatoes', 'beans'], 10)).resolves.toBe(false)`, and a second test for a yes.

tasks.title: Test an item the shed has no count for
tasks.description:
When the form asks for an item that is not in `shed.json`, `countOf` rejects with an error whose message names that item, so Effie knows what to add. In the `unknown item` block, test that it does, for an item of your own.

Check runs your tests on the working code and on versions that answer with nothing, or reject without naming the item. A test in this block must pass on the first and fail on the others.
nextSteps: Pick an item that is not in `shed.json`.
Give the promise from `countOf` to `expect`, not a function.
Use `rejects`, and check that the message names your item.
hints: `expect(() => countOf(item)).toThrow()` fails: an async function hands back a promise and never throws straight away.
`rejects` waits for the error, and `toThrow` with text after it checks the message, as in the last issue.
